C.clue: Glucocorticoid inhibiting 1-alpha-hydroxylase in lymphoma or granulomas
C.fit: Not here: indicated for calcitriol-mediated hypercalcemia, not osteolytic breast metastases
C.tempting: treats hypercalcemia of malignancy

D.clue: RNA synthesis inhibitor with severe hepatorenal toxicity
D.fit: Not here: obsolete and toxic agent; bisphosphonates preferred
D.tempting: historical agent for refractory cancer hypercalcemia

E.clue: Restores intravascular volume and promotes urinary calcium clearance
E.fit: Here: calcium 14.9 mg/dL, dry mucous membranes, lethargy

F.clue: Phosphate binder risking severe metastatic tissue calcification
F.fit: Not here: causes dangerous calcium phosphate precipitation and organ failure
F.tempting: binds serum calcium to lower blood levels

nodes.text: Serum calcium > 14 mg/dL + altered mental status, dehydration, and bone pain
Immediate aggressive IV 0.9% normal saline hydration to restore intravascular volume
Add subcutaneous calcitonin for rapid short-term calcium reduction over 24-48 hours
Administer IV bisphosphonate (zoledronic acid) for sustained long-term calcium control
**Refractory severe hypercalcemia or renal failure:** hemodialysis with low-calcium dialysate
**Volume overload develops during saline hydration:** add IV furosemide

671826.hinge: Fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, and hypotension refractory to intra-abdominal infection (perforated appendicitis) define septic shock.
671826.trap: Prior myocardial infarction might tempt cardiogenic shock, but high fever and pelvic tenderness point to intra-abdominal sepsis.

A.clue: Pump failure with elevated JVD, crackles, gallop
A.fit: Not here: no JVD, lungs clear, high fever 38.8°C
A.tempting: history of coronary artery disease and myocardial infarction

B.clue: Extrinsic vascular obstruction with pulsus paradoxus
B.fit: Not here: intra-abdominal infection source, no evidence of tamponade or PE
B.tempting: causes acute hypotension postoperatively

C.clue: Intravascular depletion from hemorrhage without infectious source
C.fit: Not here: high fever and suprapubic peritonitis indicate septic etiology
C.tempting: vomiting twice prior to presentation

D.clue: Loss of vascular tone from central cord trauma
D.fit: Not here: marked tachycardia (122/min), fever, intra-abdominal infection
D.tempting: causes distributive vasodilation and hypotension

E.clue: Systemic vasodilation from dysregulated host response to infection
E.fit: Here: perforated appendix, fever 38.8°C, pulse 122, BP 88/50 mm Hg

nodes.text: Fever + tachycardia + tachypnea + hypotension (SBP < 90 mm Hg) following abdominal surgery
Obtain blood cultures + rapid IV crystalloid resuscitation with lactated Ringer solution
Initiate empiric IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam or cefepime + metronidazole)
**Hypotension refractory to fluid resuscitation:** initiate norepinephrine as first-line vasopressor
Urgent CT scan of abdomen and pelvis to identify source (pelvic abscess or leak)
**Drainable fluid collection on CT:** percutaneous or surgical drainage

Temperature is 38.8°C (101.8°F)
pulse is 122/min, respirations are 23/min, and blood pressure is 88/50 mm Hg

671827.boardCall: Coma + absent brainstem reflexes + family requests confirmatory test for brain death -> cerebral blood flow studies
671827.hinge: Cerebral blood flow studies (cerebral angiography, radionuclide perfusion scan, or transcranial Doppler) provide definitive confirmatory testing for brain death.
671827.trap: CT or MRI shows structural brain trauma, but documentation of absent intracranial blood flow is required to confirm brain death.

A.clue: Confirms irreversible cessation of intracranial circulation
A.fit: Here: comatose, absent brainstem reflexes, apnea, family requests confirmatory test

B.clue: Anatomic imaging detecting intracranial hematoma and shift
B.fit: Not here: evaluates structural pathology but cannot prove cessation of perfusion
B.tempting: standard emergency evaluation for severe traumatic brain injury

C.clue: Measures intracranial compartment pressure via invasive transducer
C.fit: Not here: high ICP does not alone establish death of brain tissue
C.tempting: elevated ICP causes cerebral herniation

D.clue: Parenchymal magnetic resonance imaging requiring patient transport
D.fit: Not here: cannot definitively establish complete cessation of cerebral blood flow
D.tempting: provides sensitive evaluation of brainstem injury

E.clue: Plain bone radiography assessing cranial fractures
E.fit: Not here: demonstrates skull fracture without assessing brain vitality
E.tempting: patient has a depressed frontal skull fracture

nodes.text: Comatose patient with catastrophic irreversible brain injury: exclude hypothermia, drugs, and shock
Comprehensive clinical exam: coma, absent pupillary, corneal, oculocephalic, vestibulo-ocular, and gag reflexes
Apnea testing: pre-oxygenate, disconnect ventilator, observe for respiratory efforts as PaCO2 reaches >= 60 mm Hg
Ancillary testing (cerebral blood flow studies or EEG) when apnea test cannot be completed or family requests proof
**Absent cerebral blood flow on four-vessel angiography or nuclear scintigraphy:** formal legal declaration of death
Notify organ procurement organization and support family through bereavement

671828.boardCall: Competent adult patient refuses low-yield experimental therapy despite parents' objections -> respect the wishes of the patient
671828.hinge: An adult patient with decision-making capacity possesses full ethical autonomy and legal authority to refuse treatments, even life-prolonging interventions.
671828.trap: Distraught parents wanting full intervention cannot override an autonomous adult patient's informed refusal.

A.clue: Hospital ethics consultation for complex ethical conflict resolution
A.fit: Not here: autonomous adult capacity is clear; consultative override is inappropriate
A.tempting: resolves deep ethical disagreements between family and patient

B.clue: Upholds patient autonomy to refuse medical interventions
B.fit: Here: 18-year-old competent adult declining 5% survival experimental protocol

C.clue: Judicial mandate for psychiatric capacity evaluation
C.fit: Not here: wanting to refuse agonizing treatment does not indicate psychiatric incompetence
C.tempting: patient states she is ready to die

D.clue: Violates adult patient autonomy at surrogate family request
D.fit: Not here: legally an adult; parents have no surrogate authority
D.tempting: parents desire aggressive treatment to improve daughter's prognosis

algorithm.title: Adult patient autonomy and treatment refusal

nodes.text: Adult patient (age >= 18) refuses proposed life-prolonging or experimental therapy against family wishes
Assess decision-making capacity: understanding, appreciation, reasoning, and expression of a choice
Respect the competent patient's autonomous decision to decline further disease-directed therapy
**Impaired capacity without advance directive:** surrogate decision-making based on substituted judgment
Offer comprehensive palliative care and symptom management tailored to patient's goals
Facilitate open family meetings with social work and chaplaincy to support grieving parents

experimental treatment protocol that would involve bone marrow transplantation
she says that she is ready to die

abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.scope: screening recommendations (men 65-75 who smoked), ultrasound imaging, surveillance intervals, elective repair thresholds, rupture
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.core: Older adult with abdominal aortic dilation may remain asymptomatic until expansion or rupture; sudden abdominal/back pain and hypotension require immediate vascular rescue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking strongest modifiable risk; older age, male sex, family history, hypertension, atherosclerosis
Women have higher rupture risk at smaller diameters; most aneurysms infrarenal

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental pulsatile expansile abdominal mass; localized persistent pain suggests symptomatic aneurysm
Rupture triad incompletely present; transient stability may reflect contained retroperitoneal hemorrhage
Blue toe/distal ischemia may result from mural thrombus embolization

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medial elastin/collagen degradation → progressive enlargement; greater wall radius increases tension
Retroperitoneal containment can briefly limit blood loss before catastrophic decompensation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Abdominal ultrasound** diagnoses AAA, generally diameter ≥3 cm; no contrast required
★ Stable suspected rupture or preoperative planning → **CT angiography**
Unstable suspected rupture → bedside ultrasound if immediate; no CT transport delaying surgery
Ultrasound detects aneurysm but cannot reliably exclude rupture; follow symptoms/hemodynamics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Rupture → **urgent vascular repair**, IV access, blood products; avoid delaying for complete workup
Permissive hypotension during transfer/resuscitation until hemorrhage control when clinically feasible
★ Elective repair at **≥5.5 cm men, ≥5.0 cm women**, or aneurysm-attributable symptoms
Rapid growth ≥0.5 cm/6 months → repair consideration; endovascular versus open based on anatomy/fitness
Smaller asymptomatic lesions → ultrasound surveillance below; refer vascular surgery, manage cardiovascular risks

rows.label: Complications
items: Rupture, thrombosis, distal embolization; repair → AKI, bowel ischemia, endoleak after EVAR
Aortoenteric fistula after prior graft: herald GI bleed → catastrophic hemorrhage; urgent evaluation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **one-time ultrasound men 65–75 who ever smoked**; selectively screen never-smoking men
Women never smoked/no family history → no screening; women smokers/family history → USPSTF evidence insufficient
Smoking cessation, BP control, statin for atherosclerotic disease; lifelong imaging follow-up after EVAR

rows.label: Mimics
items: Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; shock atypical
Aortic dissection: abrupt chest/back pain, possible pulse deficits or branch ischemia

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, heart failure, cirrhosis; baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment injury, prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → interstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia → isotonic crystalloid; congestion → loop diuretic; avoid reflex fluids in overloaded patients
Stop culprit nephrotoxins; renal-dose drugs; AIN persisting after withdrawal → consider glucocorticoids
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; lactation and milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: painless postlactational mass; fat–fluid level on imaging
Abscess: focal tender erythematous fluctuant mass, sometimes fever; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → papilloma or malignancy evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Simple painful cyst → aspiration; bloody fluid or residual mass → further tissue evaluation
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID; galactocele → aspiration if symptomatic
★ Abscess → ultrasound-guided drainage + **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**; MRSA risk → clindamycin
Continue breastfeeding/pumping with lactational infection; persistent pathologic discharge → breast surgical evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

bowel-obstruction.name: Bowel obstruction
bowel-obstruction.scope: Small bowel obstruction (adhesions, hernia), large bowel obstruction (volvulus, malignancy), paralytic ileus, NG decompression, surgical management
bowel-obstruction.core: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, distention, and obstipation suggest mechanical obstruction; constant pain or systemic toxicity raises concern for strangulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior abdominal surgery, incarcerated hernia, Crohn strictures → small-bowel obstruction
Colorectal malignancy, chronic constipation, institutionalization → large-bowel obstruction or sigmoid volvulus
Recent surgery, opioids, hypokalemia, severe systemic illness → ileus

rows.label: Clues
items: Early high-pitched sounds may become absent; proximal obstruction causes earlier vomiting, distal disease greater distention
★ **Peritonitis, fever, tachycardia, rising lactate**, or continuous severe pain → ischemia/perforation
Partial obstruction may still permit stool or diarrhea; bowel movements do not exclude early obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal blockage → upstream dilation, third spacing; closed loop compromises venous then arterial supply
Adynamic ileus reflects impaired motility without an anatomic transition point

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** defines transition point, cause, and ischemic signs
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, lactate; normal lactate cannot exclude early ischemia
Radiograph may show dilated loops/air-fluid levels; CT more definitive if diagnosis uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **NPO, IV isotonic fluids, electrolyte correction**; NG decompression for significant vomiting/distention
★ Strangulation, perforation, closed loop, or incarcerated hernia → **urgent surgery** + ceftriaxone/metronidazole
Uncomplicated adhesive SBO → surgical observation, serial examination; water-soluble contrast helps predict resolution
Failure to improve during a short monitored trial, commonly up to 72 h → operation
Ileus → correct trigger, reduce opioids, mobilize; no operation solely for absent sounds

rows.label: Complications
items: Dehydration, AKI, hypokalemic alkalosis; bowel necrosis, perforation, sepsis
Recurrent adhesions; short-bowel syndrome after extensive resection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early postoperative ambulation, opioid-sparing analgesia, electrolyte correction; elective repair of symptomatic hernias

rows.label: Mimics
items: Gastroenteritis: prominent diarrhea, no focal transition point
Mesenteric ischemia: pain out of proportion before peritoneal signs

bowel-obstruction.evidence: Not checked online; established acute surgical management principles.

brain-death.name: Brain death
brain-death.scope: Prerequisites (normothermia, normal BP), clinical exam (coma, absent brainstem reflexes), apnea test, ancillary testing (cerebral blood flow studies)
brain-death.core: Permanent loss of all brain function, including brainstem function, constitutes death; a beating heart on ventilation does not negate the diagnosis.

rows.label: Principle
items: Known catastrophic irreversible brain injury; compatible neuroimaging; adequate observation period

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Prerequisites: **temperature ≥36°C**, adult SBP ≥100 and MAP ≥75 mm Hg
Exclude paralysis/metabolic confounders; sedatives: ≥5 half-lives, longer if impaired clearance
★ Examination: **coma**, no brain-mediated motor response; absent brainstem reflexes (table)

rows.label: Don't
items: Oculocephalic testing with possible cervical injury; use caloric testing after confirming ear integrity
Declare death with any brain-mediated response or spontaneous breath
Use ancillary testing to bypass hypothermia or high CNS-depressant levels

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Spinal reflex movements may persist without contradicting diagnosis
Incomplete examination or unsafe apnea test → radionuclide cerebral perfusion or catheter angiography
After temperature ≤35.5°C, wait ≥24 hours following rewarming to ≥36°C

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Apnea test: no breaths, **PaCO2 ≥60 and ≥20 above baseline**, pH <7.30
Preoxygenate; abort apnea testing for hypotension, hypoxemia or unstable arrhythmia
★ 2023 update: **EEG no longer accepted** as ancillary testing; pediatric requirements differ

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, family history, prior chest irradiation
Prolonged estrogen exposure, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative breast lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core needle biopsy of suspicious lesion
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; locally advanced: neoadjuvant systemic treatment then surgery/radiation
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment; monitor LVEF
Triple-negative → chemotherapy; selected higher-risk disease → pembrolizumab-containing regimen
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone, lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

burn-injuries.name: Burn injuries
burn-injuries.scope: Superficial, partial-thickness, full-thickness burns, total body surface area (Rule of Nines), fluid resuscitation (Parkland), smoke inhalation and airway edema, carbon monoxide/cyanide toxicity
burn-injuries.core: Burn severity depends on depth, affected surface area, location, and inhalation injury; airway threats and hypovolemia take priority over wound care.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Flames/scalds, electricity, chemicals; closed-space fires increase toxic inhalation risk
Older adults, children, impaired mobility/sensation; inconsistent injury history raises abuse concern

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Hoarseness, stridor, oropharyngeal edema, soot** → threatened airway; skin burns may appear minor
CO: headache, confusion, syncope despite normal pulse oximetry
Cyanide: enclosed-fire exposure with cardiovascular collapse and severe lactic acidosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Capillary leak → intravascular depletion and edema; swelling progresses after initial presentation
CO impairs oxygen transport; cyanide blocks mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TBSA excludes superficial burns**; adult Rule of Nines: head/each arm 9%, each leg 18%
Anterior/posterior trunk 18% each, perineum 1%; own palm including fingers ≈1%; children → Lund-Browder
★ Inhalation/toxin concern → **ABG with co-oximetry**, lactate; normal PaO2 does not exclude CO
Electrical burn → ECG, CK, urinalysis for rhabdomyolysis; small surface injury may hide deep damage

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway threat → **intubate**; burn center: full-thickness, ≥10% partial, critical-site, inhalation/electrical/chemical
CO → 100% oxygen; severe neurologic/cardiac toxicity or pregnancy → consider hyperbaric oxygen; cyanide → hydroxocobalamin
Lactated Ringer: classic **Parkland = 4 mL × kg × %TBSA** during first 24 hours
Half by 8 hours from injury, remainder over 16; ABA now starts adults at 2 mL/kg/%TBSA

rows.label: Complications
items: Shock, AKI, infection, contractures, compartment syndrome; overresuscitation worsens edema
Restrictive chest/limb eschar → escharotomy; true compartment syndrome → fasciotomy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Titrate fluids to urine output ≥0.5 mL/kg/hour in adults; formula only starting estimate
Analgesia, cleaning, moist nonadherent dressings, tetanus; avoid routine systemic antibiotic prophylaxis
★ **Stop exposure, remove jewelry, cool water**, prevent hypothermia; no ice
Smoke/CO detectors, safe water temperature, fire escape plan; early rehabilitation and range of motion

rows.label: Mimics
items: SJS/TEN: medication exposure, mucosal erosions, widespread epidermal detachment
Cellulitis: spreading warmth/erythema without immediate thermal exposure

table.title: Depth
rows: Moist blisters, brisk blanching, very painful

burn-injuries.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ABA burn resuscitation guideline 2024](https://academic.oup.com/jbcr/article/45/3/565/7458089); classic Parkland contrasted with current initial estimate.

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.name: Catheter-related bloodstream infection
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.scope: Central line infection, organisms, line removal, prevention
catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.core: Fever or rigors in a patient with an intravascular catheter, especially during infusion, raises concern for catheter-related bacteremia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long catheter dwell time, femoral placement, parenteral nutrition, immunosuppression, hemodialysis
Poor asepsis, frequent hub manipulation; tunneled devices and ports also susceptible

rows.label: Clues
items: Exit-site erythema or drainage may occur; normal insertion-site appearance does not exclude infection
★ **Hypotension, persistent bacteremia**, new murmur, or embolic signs → complicated infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Skin flora migrate externally or contaminated hubs seed intraluminal biofilm
Biofilm limits antibiotic penetration; S aureus and Candida frequently seed distant sites

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Before antibiotics: **paired peripheral and catheter blood cultures**, labelled by source
Same organism with catheter culture positive ≥2 h earlier supports catheter source
Culture removed catheter tip when infection suspected; no routine tip culture after elective removal
Repeat blood cultures to document clearance; persistent positivity → endocarditis, infected thrombus, abscess evaluation
S aureus bacteremia → echocardiography, TEE when high risk; assess metastatic foci

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sepsis → **IV vancomycin + cefepime**, adjusted to cultures and local resistance
★ **Remove line** for shock, tunnel infection, endocarditis, persistent bacteremia, S aureus, Pseudomonas, or fungi
Candida → echinocandin; MSSA → cefazolin or nafcillin; enterococcal treatment follows susceptibilities
Selected stable long-term line infections with coagulase-negative staphylococci → systemic antibiotics + antibiotic lock
Uncomplicated S aureus bacteremia: ≥14 days after clearance; endocarditis/deep infection usually requires 4–6 weeks

rows.label: Complications
items: Endocarditis, septic thrombophlebitis, osteomyelitis, septic emboli, shock
Unnecessary device retention → relapse; repeated placement → thrombosis and vascular injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Hand hygiene, chlorhexidine skin preparation, maximal sterile barrier** during insertion
Scrub hubs, sterile dressings, daily necessity review, prompt removal of unnecessary lines
Avoid routine prophylactic systemic antibiotics or scheduled catheter replacement solely to prevent infection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Contaminated blood culture: single skin-flora isolate without corroborating cultures or illness
Infusate reaction: temporal symptoms without reproducible bacteremia
Catheter thrombosis: swelling, poor flow; cultures negative unless infected

table.title: Organism pattern
rows: Parenteral nutrition, broad antibiotics; remove catheter

catheter-related-bloodstream-infection.evidence: Not checked online; established catheter-infection management principles.

cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.name: Cirrhosis and portal hypertension
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.scope: Ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, hepatic encephalopathy, esophageal varices, hepatorenal syndrome, hepatocellular carcinoma screening
cirrhosis-and-portal-hypertension.core: Cirrhosis produces portal hypertension and synthetic failure; new ascites, bleeding, confusion or kidney injury signals decompensation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Alcohol, chronic HBV/HCV, metabolic steatotic liver disease; autoimmune/cholestatic disorders

rows.label: Clues
items: Splenomegaly, thrombocytopenia, spider angiomas, jaundice, muscle wasting
Encephalopathy triggers: GI bleeding, infection, constipation, sedatives, hypokalemia
SBP may present only with subtle confusion or renal deterioration; fever/pain can be absent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fibrosis raises intrahepatic resistance; splanchnic vasodilation lowers effective arterial volume
Portal collaterals bleed; impaired toxin clearance causes neuropsychiatric dysfunction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ New/worsening or hospitalized ascites → **diagnostic paracentesis**; PMN **≥250/µL** → treat SBP
SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL supports portal hypertension; send ascitic culture in bedside blood-culture bottles
HRS-AKI: exclude shock, nephrotoxins, obstruction and structural injury; assess volume response
MELD-Na/MELD 3.0 guides prognosis/transplant assessment; ammonia does not establish encephalopathy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Variceal bleed → resuscitate, **octreotide + ceftriaxone**, urgent endoscopic banding; refractory → TIPS
Ascites → sodium restriction, spironolactone ± furosemide; tense ascites → paracentesis, albumin if >5 L
★ SBP → **ceftriaxone**, albumin for high-risk renal/liver dysfunction; reassess response
Encephalopathy → lactulose to 2–3 soft stools/day; recurrent episodes → add rifaximin; correct trigger
HRS → stop diuretics/nephrotoxins, **terlipressin + albumin** after volume assessment; monitor hypoxia; transplant evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: HCC, recurrent infection, malnutrition, hepatopulmonary syndrome; TIPS can worsen encephalopathy
Avoid NSAIDs, sedatives and unnecessary fluid loading; INR alone poorly predicts procedural bleeding

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Ultrasound + AFP every 6 months** for HCC surveillance in eligible cirrhosis
Carvedilol for clinically significant portal hypertension when tolerated; banding if indicated and beta blocker unsuitable
After SBP → antibiotic prophylaxis; alcohol abstinence, hepatitis vaccines, adequate protein intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cardiac ascites: high SAAG with ascitic protein ≥2.5 g/dL
Malignant/TB ascites: usually low SAAG

colorectal-carcinoma.name: Colorectal carcinoma
colorectal-carcinoma.scope: Colon adenocarcinoma, rectal cancer, staging, surgical resection (hemicolectomy), liver metastases, chemotherapy
colorectal-carcinoma.core: Occult blood loss, altered bowel habits, or obstruction warrants colon evaluation; cancer stage determines local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, adenomas, Lynch/FAP, longstanding colitis, family history; smoking, obesity, processed meat

rows.label: Clues
items: Right-sided lesions → iron-deficiency anemia, fatigue, occult bleeding
Left-sided lesions → constipation, narrowed stools, obstruction; rectal lesions → tenesmus/hematochezia
Weight loss, palpable mass; hepatomegaly or elevated ALP suggests hepatic spread

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Adenoma–carcinoma sequence involves APC, KRAS, p53; mismatch-repair failure drives microsatellite instability
Portal drainage favors liver metastases; distal rectal tumors may spread directly to lungs

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Colonoscopy with biopsy**; evaluate entire colon for synchronous tumors
★ Confirmed cancer → **CT chest/abdomen/pelvis**, baseline CEA, tumor mismatch-repair/MSI testing
Rectal cancer → pelvic MRI for local staging; CEA cannot diagnose or screen
Obstruction/perforation → urgent contrast CT and surgical assessment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Resectable colon cancer → **segmental colectomy with lymphadenectomy**
Stage III → adjuvant FOLFOX/CAPOX; selected high-risk stage II → individualized chemotherapy
Locally advanced rectal cancer → neoadjuvant systemic chemotherapy/chemoradiation, then total mesorectal excision
MSI-high advanced disease → checkpoint inhibitor; selected liver metastases → resection after multidisciplinary assessment
Perforation or unstable obstruction → urgent operation; selected stable obstruction → stent or diversion

rows.label: Complications
items: Bleeding, perforation, malignant obstruction; venous thrombosis; oxaliplatin neuropathy
Postoperative anastomotic leak; pelvic treatment → urinary/sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Average-risk screening **45–75 years**; earlier colonoscopy for strong family history/hereditary syndromes
Postresection colonoscopy, CEA and stage-based CT surveillance; remove premalignant polyps

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hemorrhoids: outlet bleeding without explanatory anemia; do not dismiss alarm features
IBD: chronic inflammatory diarrhea; diverticulitis: acute focal pain and fever

colorectal-carcinoma.evidence: Screening checked 2026-10-30: [USPSTF colorectal screening](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/colorectal-cancer-screening); treatment: established oncology teaching.
